source: WFScript RC1.5.14.10.8, API unchanged from source-verified 10.4 public catalog; behavior updates noted

entries.name: ui.set
entries.args: Panel widget ID and runtime value
entries.description: Measurement Result: numeric ui.set evaluates configured min/max inclusive, {reset:true} clears. Measurement Table: array of {name,value,unit,low,high}, or {reset:true}. Event Log: {append:{level,message,source?,timestamp?}}, {append:[entries...]}, full array to replace, or {clear:true}. Levels: DEBUG,INFO,PASS,WARN,FAIL,ERROR. GUI filter/Copy/Clear/Export CSV; timestamps default to local time; maxEntries bounds history, live entries not saved. Test Sequence: array of unique {id,name,description?,status?,message?,elapsedMs?} (maxSteps property), {update:{id,status?,message?,elapsedMs?,name?,description?}}, {reset:true} (retain steps, reset states), or {clear:true}. States: pending,running,pass,done,fail,error,skipped,aborted. The Test Sequence is a VIEW; the native TestRunner (if used) owns scheduling, statuses, deadlines and results. Direct ui.set() can still update a standalone sequence widget without TestRunner. Invalid updates are ignored atomically and logged to Qt warnings. ui.set confirms a known widget ID, not per-widget payload validation. Conversion from JS objects to native Qt values occurs on the script thread. Hidden Pages are updated; runtime values are NOT persisted to .wfpanel. See Examples > Getting Started > Automated Test Station.

entries.name: ui.get
entries.description: Returns standard JavaScript primitives, arrays and plain objects (including true nested Array rows for Experiment Data Tables). No Qt QVariantList conversion is necessary: Array.isArray(ui.get("recipeTable")) is true. A returned array/object is a snapshot; call ui.set() to commit changes. Reads the most recently assigned value from the persistent Panel runtime, even when the widget is on a hidden Page. Test Sequence initially returns its configured pending steps; subsequent ui.get reads the last payload sent to ui.set, not a merged or evaluated full sequence snapshot. Measurement Result starts as null; Measurement Table and Event Log start as empty arrays. ui.get(eventLogId) returns the last ui.set payload, not the complete accumulated log or any rows cleared from the GUI. For complete examples, open Examples > Getting Started > Automated Test Station.

entries.name: ui.on
entries.description: Panel-only scripting event subscription. Use the exact saved event name (for example, clicked or valueChanged); a button uses clicked, not click. Alternatively configure handlers in the visual Events editor.

entries.name: ui.tableRowCount
entries.description: Read retained Experiment DataTable row count; returns -1 for an unknown table. Example: ui.tableRowCount("experimentTable");

entries.name: ui.tableSlice
entries.description: Read up to 2048 retained rows by zero-based indexes; does not clone the full table. Example: ui.tableSlice("experimentTable",0,10);

entries.name: ui.tableRow
entries.description: Convenience bounded read of one row, or null when invalid. Example: var row=ui.tableRow("experimentTable",0);

entries.name: ui.tableSelection
entries.description: Read cached selection {row,column,rows,selectedCells,truncated}; selected row list capped at 128. The selectionChanged event updates this state.

entries.name: ui.tableSetTitle
entries.description: Sets runtime toolbar title (max 120 characters); does not save as Designer property.

entries.name: ui.tableSetStatus
entries.description: Sets optional runtime status line (max 200 characters).

entries.name: ui.tableFollow
entries.description: Sets whether newest rows are followed when the view is already at its bottom; retains browsing position otherwise.

entries.name: ui.tableImportCsv
entries.description: Requests CSV import by dialog or specified path. Return indicates command acceptance, NOT file completion. Use importCompleted event.

entries.name: ui.tableExportCsv
entries.description: Requests CSV export by dialog or specified path. Return indicates command acceptance, NOT file completion. Use exportCompleted event.

entries.name: ui.tableCopySelection
entries.description: Copies selected cells as tab-separated values; use Export CSV for large datasets.

entries.name: Data.get
entries.description: Project-owned shared variables span all Pages. Unknown name throws. Values reset to saved initial defaults each Run; no automatic hardware operation or disk logging.

entries.name: Data.set
entries.args: Declared name and value matching Number/Boolean/Text type
entries.description: Automatically refreshes every compatible Value-bound widget on all Pages, without triggering a user event. Invalid type or missing name throws. Direct ui.set on a bound widget throws; for unbound widgets ui.set is unchanged.

entries.name: Data.names
entries.description: Lists variables defined under Properties → Panel Data, not files in the shared PanelData directory. Design-time initial values and live Run values are separate.

entries.name: Data.onChange
entries.args: Declared variable name, function(value,previousValue,name), optional immediate
entries.description: Fires synchronously after successful, changed Data.set or compatible operator Value Binding edits. No notification for equal writes, initial project defaults, or invalid values. immediate:true invokes once on registration with previousValue undefined. Listeners may call Data.set; queued delivery avoids recursive stack growth and caps a feedback cycle at 256 events. Throws for invalid arguments or when 256 listeners are active. Callback errors appear in Panel diagnostics without stopping other subscribers. Returns an integer subscription ID valid until Stop.

entries.name: Data.offChange
entries.description: Removes a previously registered listener. Returns true only once; false for unknown/removed IDs. Subscriptions are cleared automatically when the Panel stops. No physical outputs or I/O occur automatically.

entries.name: Data.computed
entries.example:
// Declare Motor.TargetRPS as Number in Properties → Panel Data first.
Data.computed('Motor.TargetRPS',['Motor.TargetRPM'],function(rpm){return rpm/60;});
entries.args: Predeclared target variable; array of 1..16 declared dependency names; pure function(...values)
entries.description: Registers one typed, read-only runtime formula. Recomputes synchronously in topological order when any declared dependency changes, including bound operator inputs. Values propagate to bound displays and Data.onChange; source listeners see updated derived values. Dependencies must be explicit; formulas cannot call Data.set or register additional computed values. Up to 64 formulas. Duplicate targets, missing dependencies, editable output bindings and dependency cycles are rejected. Formula exceptions/invalid outputs are reported; previous derived values are retained. All computed definitions reset on Stop.

entries.name: Data.isComputed
entries.description: Returns true if Data.computed registered the declared variable for this Panel run. Computed values are read-only via Data.set and native input. Unknown names throw. All definitions must still exist in Properties → Panel Data to allow design-time widget binding.

entries.name: modules.load
entries.description: Uses Qt native ECMAScript modules; same engine, with cached exports. Embedded panel libraries take priority over shared files.

entries.name: modules.userFolder
entries.description: Shows the writable per-user library folder. Manage modules via Script > Manage Script Libraries.

entries.name: include
entries.description: Runs a classic script once per engine in global scope. Use modules.load() for native .mjs exports.

entries.name: print
entries.description: Prints to the Script output console.

entries.name: wait
entries.description: This is the script delay helper, not Scope.wait().

entries.name: setTimeout
entries.args: Callable function; integer delay 10..86400000 ms; optional callback arguments    Units: ms
entries.description: Panel scripts only. Schedules one callback; removed from active timers before invocation. Uses Qt event-loop timing; no guaranteed execution deadline. Does not block onInitialize() or other scripts. An invalid delay throws a script error.

entries.name: clearTimeout
entries.args: Timer ID returned by setTimeout(); an unknown ID is harmless
entries.description: Cancels an outstanding one-shot timer. Safe when called after it has already fired. Automatic cleanup prevents callbacks after Panel stop and restart.

entries.name: setInterval
entries.args: Callable function; integer interval 10..86400000 ms; optional callback arguments    Units: ms
entries.description: Panel scripts only. A native Qt QTimer on the PanelRuntime/QJSEngine thread schedules repeat callbacks; each call creates an independent timer. At most 256 active timers. No overlap: long synchronous JavaScript delays this timer, UART polling and TestRunner. Invalid delays and over-capacity requests throw script errors. Not a real-time clock.

entries.name: clearInterval
entries.args: Timer ID returned by setInterval(); an unknown ID is harmless
entries.description: Cancels a repeating timer immediately; can be called inside its callback. All timers are cancelled when the Panel stops. Cancelled IDs are not reused in the same Panel run.

entries.name: Device.isConnected
entries.description: A connected AD3 or the selected simulation can satisfy this query.

entries.name: Scope1.single
entries.description: Arms an acquisition. Call Scope.wait() to obtain completed data.

entries.name: Scope1.wait
entries.args: Optional timeout in seconds    Units: s
entries.description: Checks acquisition completion. Do not assume data is ready before the wait succeeds.

entries.name: Scope1.Time.Rate.value
entries.description: Actual supported rate depends on AD3 configuration.

entries.name: Scope1.Time.Samples.value
entries.args: Requested acquisition buffer size    Units: samples
entries.description: For larger captures, use Scope Record mode if supported.

entries.name: Scope1.Channel1.Range.value
entries.args: Requested oscilloscope range in peak-to-peak volts    Units: Vpp
entries.description: Existing WaveForms-style property. Hardware may round or map requested Vpp to an available gain/range. Call Scope1.config() or single() before checking Range.real.

entries.name: Scope1.Channel1.Range.real
entries.args: Read-only effective range, following successful config/single    Units: Vpp
entries.description: Reads FDwfAnalogInChannelRangeGet for actual hardware configuration. In simulation the readback equals the requested range. Do not interpret as an extra physical gain stage.

entries.name: Scope1.Channel1.Range.steps
entries.args: Read-only SDK-advertised selectable ranges    Units: Vpp
entries.description: Read from FDwfAnalogInChannelRangeSteps when the device is opened. [] means no reported values, including in simulation; see Scope1.capabilities().rangeStepsAvailable. These are selectable settings, not separate hardware amplifier gains.

entries.name: Scope1.capabilities
entries.example:
var c=Scope1.capabilities();
print(c.rangeStepsAvailable, c.rangeSteps, c.rangeMinVpp, c.rangeMaxVpp);
entries.args: No arguments    Units: Vpp and other units
entries.description: Includes device-advertised rangeSteps, rangeStepsAvailable, rangeMinVpp, rangeMaxVpp and rangeStepCount where the SDK exposes them. Range discovery is non-mutating and optional.

entries.name: Scope1.Channel1.measure
entries.args: Measurement name, optional start/end seconds    Units: Depends on measurement
entries.description: Computes from the last completed capture. Ctrl+Space after the opening quote suggests measurement names.

entries.name: Scope1.Channel1.measureWindow
entries.args: Measurement name, start/end times (seconds)    Units: Depends on measurement
entries.description: Time bounds must be ordered and fit the capture.

entries.name: Scope1.Channel1.measureCapture
entries.args: Measurement name, optional time bounds    Units: Depends on measurement
entries.description: Uses captured sample data, not a live hardware query.

entries.name: Scope1.Channel1.spectrum
entries.args: Power-of-two FFT size, window: Hann, Rectangular, Blackman    Units: Hz, V
entries.description: Returns numeric spectrum data. Frequency and amplitude depend on window and sampling conditions.

entries.name: Scope1.Channel1.statistics
entries.example:
var stats = Scope.Channel1.statistics();
print(stats.rms, stats.min, stats.max);
entries.args: Optional start and end times    Units: mixed
entries.description: Computes measurements in native C++ from the last capture.

entries.name: Scope1.captureInfo
entries.description: Host-after-transfer timestamp differs from the DWF trigger timestamp.

entries.name: Scope1.saveReference
entries.description: Copies the last completed channel buffer; reference persists across captures.

entries.name: Scope1.mathData
entries.args: CH1-CH2, CH1+CH2, CH1*CH2, CH1-REF1, CH2-REF2    Units: Varies
entries.description: Requires matching sample counts; reference math also requires matching sampling rates.

entries.name: Scope1.Time.Mode.text
entries.args: Repeated, Shift, Record, or hardware-supported mode
entries.description: Some modes are unavailable on certain hardware; check Scope.capabilities().

entries.name: Wavegen1.run
entries.description: Configures and starts enabled waveform generators. Changes physical outputs in Hardware mode.

entries.name: Wavegen1.stop
entries.description: Stops the generator.

entries.name: Wavegen1.Channel1.enable
entries.description: Selects whether a generator channel is enabled.

entries.name: Wavegen1.Channel1.Simple.Frequency.value
entries.description: Effective output range depends on the device configuration.

entries.name: Wavegen1.Channel1.Simple.Amplitude.value
entries.args: Amplitude in volts (peak)    Units: V peak
entries.description: The generated sine wave has approximately 0.707 V RMS at 1 V peak.

entries.name: Wavegen1.Channel1.Simple.Offset.value
entries.description: Output voltage limits depend on range and offset combined.

entries.name: Wavegen1.Channel1.Simple.Type.text
entries.description: Use autocomplete inside quotes for available choices; selected hardware may restrict them.

entries.name: Wavegen1.Channel1.Mode.text
entries.description: Use autocomplete inside quotes for supported modes.

entries.name: Wavegen1.Channel1.Modulation.FM.enable
entries.description: Enabling FM changes generator output; check supported hardware modes.

entries.name: Wavegen1.play
entries.description: For finite streaming playback after filling the Play buffer.

entries.name: Supplies.run
entries.description: Explicitly turns master on and commits both output channels. Power is OFF at Panel/script completion. No output is energized in simulation.

entries.name: Supplies.config
entries.description: Commits the staged WaveForms-style settings; unlike WaveForms' UI-backed properties, WFScript requires an explicit commit. Invalid settings fail closed.

entries.name: Supplies.stop
entries.description: Disables AD3 supply master; the script and Panel runtime also call stop on cleanup if supplies were used.

entries.name: Supplies.status
entries.example:
var s = Supplies.status();
print(s.measuredAvailable, s.positiveVoltage, s.negativeVoltage);
entries.description: Reads AD3 AnalogIO status. measuredAvailable=false means no physical voltage readback; simulation values are ideal and not measurements.

entries.name: Supplies.MasterEnable.checked
entries.description: WaveForms-compatible master enable property. Staged until config(); run() also turns on master.

entries.name: Supplies.Output.PositiveSupply.Enable.value
entries.description: V+ channel enabled only if master is also on. Changes require config()/run().

entries.name: Supplies.Output.NegativeSupply.Enable.value
entries.description: V- channel enabled only if master is also on. Changes require config()/run().

entries.name: Supplies.Output.PositiveSupply.Voltage.value
entries.description: AD3 voltage command, bounded; changes are staged until config()/run().

entries.name: Supplies.Output.NegativeSupply.Voltage.value
entries.description: Negative rail signed voltage. Both setpoints must remain in range, even when output disabled.

entries.name: Supplies.Output.PositiveSupply.Voltage.real
entries.description: Most recent SDK voltage status, not guaranteed accurate if readback unavailable. Check status().measuredAvailable.

entries.name: Supplies.Output.NegativeSupply.Voltage.real
entries.description: Most recent SDK voltage status; check status().measuredAvailable. Simulation reports an ideal model.

entries.name: StaticIO.onChange
entries.args: pin 0..15, callback(value,pin,event), edge change/rising/falling, debounce 0..1000 ms
entries.description: Registers or replaces one callback on a digital input WITHOUT starting polling. Host-observed transitions after stable debounce only. Event timestamps are HOST-poll times, not hardware-captured edge times. Panel scripts only.

entries.name: StaticIO.startMonitor
entries.description: Opt-in only: obtains an initial snapshot, then uses one Qt timer and one read-only DigitalIOStatus/InputStatus snapshot per poll for all 16 pins. Does not drive outputs, reset instruments or alter Scope/Wavegen configuration. SDK/USB contention and JS delays remain possible.

entries.name: StaticIO.stopMonitor
entries.description: Stops Qt polling immediately without modifying outputs. Registered callbacks stay available for an explicit later startMonitor(). clearOnChange/clearAllOnChange unregister them.

entries.name: StaticIO.clearOnChange
entries.description: Unregister the callback for one pin. Does not automatically stop the monitor.

entries.name: StaticIO.clearAllOnChange
entries.description: Remove all input-change callbacks. Polling remains active until stopMonitor() is explicitly called.

entries.name: StaticIO.monitorStats
entries.args: No arguments    Units: polls, callbacks, changes, lastPollDurationUs
entries.description: Host-side polling and callback diagnostics. Polling is NOT a real-time hardware edge detector; pulses shorter than the poll interval may be missed. An SDK error stops the monitor and never fabricates an input event.

entries.name: StaticIO.monitoring
entries.description: True only while the opt-in input monitor's native Qt timer is running. Monitoring is off by default and stopped on Panel shutdown.

entries.name: StaticIO.config
entries.description: WFScript explicitly commits staged pin values; unlike the WaveForms Static I/O GUI, property assignment alone does not drive the pin. Disabled pins default to Z.

entries.name: StaticIO.setPin
entries.description: WFScript convenience method that updates and commits one pin; changes hardware outputs in Physical Device mode.

entries.name: StaticIO.readPin
entries.description: Performs a new DigitalIOStatus snapshot before reading the input bit. -1 means failure; check StaticIO.lastError.

entries.name: StaticIO.readGroup
entries.description: Reads all 8 pins in the group in one snapshot; -1 means an SDK error.

entries.name: StaticIO.status
entries.description: Read-only DigitalIO snapshot. inputMask is actual hardware digital levels; a simulation returns ideal output echo with undriven inputs LOW.

entries.name: StaticIO.capabilities
entries.description: Queries SDK capabilities without changing directions. 0xffff is the ideal simulation mask. availability is device-dependent.

entries.name: StaticIO.stop
entries.description: Releases the StaticIO output-enable mask to 0 (all high impedance). Runtime performs cleanup if StaticIO was touched; failure to confirm high-Z is warned.

entries.name: StaticIO.Channel0.DIO0.value
entries.description: WaveForms-compatible property; this WFScript subset deliberately stages assignments until config(). DIO8..15 live under Channel1.

entries.name: StaticIO.Channel0.DIO0.text
entries.description: Invalid text is rejected on commit. Staged output state is separate from physical input state.

entries.name: StaticIO.Channel0.DIO0.Input.value
entries.description: Fresh SDK snapshot of the pin's actual logic level. Returns -1 for SDK error, not a fabricated LOW.

entries.name: StaticIO.Channel1.DIO8.value
entries.description: Channel1 contains DIO8..15. Outputs default to high impedance.

entries.name: StaticIO.Channel1.DIO8.Input.value
entries.description: Fresh input level for DIO8. Use StaticIO.status() to read all pins efficiently.

entries.name: StaticIO.Channel0.Input.value
entries.description: Eight-bit input mask for DIO0..7. SDK read error returns -1.

entries.name: StaticIO.Channel1.Input.value
entries.description: Eight-bit input mask for DIO8..15. SDK read error returns -1.

entries.name: Patterns1.runSequence
entries.args: 1..3 distinct DIO pins; 2..1024 bits/channel; 10..1,000,000 logical bits/s    Units: bits/s
entries.description: WFScript-specific extension, not a native WaveForms script method. The first character in each string is generated first, all strings must contain only 0/1 and be equal length. One shared DigitalOut start and divider keep channels aligned. Repeats continuously until stop(); SDK range and buffer limits are discovered at runtime. All output pins return to high-Z on stop. For tests connect DIO0->DIO3, DIO1->DIO4, DIO2->DIO5 through separate 1k resistors.

entries.name: Patterns1.configSequence
entries.args: Same arguments as runSequence    Units: bits/s
entries.description: Configure repeating multi-pin custom DigitalOut buffers but do not start them. Call runSequence to start. Stop releases owned outputs to high impedance.

entries.name: Patterns1.runEncoder
entries.signature: runEncoder(aPin, bPin, indexPin, ppr, rpm, reverse) : boolean
entries.args: Three distinct DIO pins 0..15; 1..1024 PPR; 1..10000 RPM; reverse boolean    Units: PPR, RPM
entries.description: WFScript-specific convenience extension: generates coherent Gray-code quadrature A/B and one index pulse per revolution using one common DigitalOut start. Hardware custom buffer must hold 4*PPR bits on ALL three channels. Direction changes require stop/restart. Call stop() to release all three outputs to Z. Use a 3-resistor DIO0->3, 1->4, 2->5 loopback for physical verification.

entries.name: Patterns1.configEncoder
entries.signature: configEncoder(aPin, bPin, indexPin, ppr, rpm, reverse) : boolean
entries.args: Same arguments as runEncoder    Units: PPR, RPM
entries.description: Load synchronized encoder data without starting the output. Explicit runEncoder() starts. Not a native WaveForms scripting method: WFScript extension.

entries.name: Patterns1.Channels.DIO1.DIO.value
entries.description: Second logical channel for an encoder B phase; last configured physical pin readback.

entries.name: Patterns1.Channels.DIO2.DIO.value
entries.description: Third logical channel for index output; last configured physical pin readback.

entries.name: Patterns1.run
entries.description: Starts one native DigitalOut Clock pattern. Explicit start only; no output when the Panel loads. Return output to high-Z with stop().

entries.name: Patterns1.config
entries.description: Stages and commits DigitalOut without starting generation. Output idle state is Z.

entries.name: Patterns1.stop
entries.description: Stops the pattern generator and disables the owned channel output. The runtime attempts stop at script/Panel exit.

entries.name: Patterns1.status
entries.args: No arguments    Units: Hz and percent
entries.description: Returns cached running/mode plus the SDK-read sdkStateName, sdkStateCode, sdkRunning, sdkRepeatCount (0=infinite), sdkStatusAvailable, sdkRepeatAvailable and achieved encoder RPM or sequence bit rate. Sequence status includes sequencePins, sequenceBitStrings, sequenceLength, sequenceActualBitRateHz and sequenceRepeatFactor. sdkRepeatCount is diagnostic only and may be nonzero despite continuous Run=0. Native fields are optional and distinguish actual DigitalOut from the cached workflow flag.

entries.name: Patterns1.Channels.DIO0.DIO.value
entries.args: Physical AD3 pin index 0..15    Units: pin
entries.description: WaveForms-compatible physical pin selector. Synonym for WFScript Pin.value; one clock/PWM channel in this revision.

entries.name: Patterns1.Channels.DIO0.Pin.value
entries.description: One logical WaveForms-style Pattern channel selects a physical pin. For custom 1..3 channel bit sequences use Patterns1.runSequence().

entries.name: Patterns1.Channels.DIO0.Type.text
entries.description: Clock uses run(); Custom is readback after runEncoder() or runSequence(). The array-based multi-channel sequencer is a WFScript extension.

entries.name: Patterns1.Channels.DIO0.Output.text
entries.description: Push-pull only; requires 3.3-V-safe hardware and no external drivers on the selected pin.

entries.name: Patterns1.Channels.DIO0.Idle.text
entries.description: High-impedance idle state. Explicit stop also disables the Pattern channel output.

entries.name: Patterns1.Channels.DIO0.Frequency.value
entries.description: Clock frequency. Achieved frequency is returned by Frequency.real after configuring.

entries.name: Patterns1.Channels.DIO0.Frequency.real
entries.description: Achieved DigitalOut counter/divider frequency from the SDK-reported base clock, not a measured signal.

entries.name: Patterns1.Channels.DIO0.Duty.value
entries.description: Duty percentage; achieved value may differ after integer counter rounding.

entries.name: Patterns1.Channels.DIO0.Duty.real
entries.description: Achieved DigitalOut counter setting; physical duty is measured separately through Logic1.

entries.name: Logic1.single
entries.description: Starts an untriggered 16-bit acquisition. This function returns after arming; call wait() to finish and transfer samples. No digital output is driven.

entries.name: Logic1.wait
entries.description: Waits until acquisition Done and loads the 16-bit sample words. Returns false on timeout or stop.

entries.name: Logic1.captureDiagnostics
entries.args: No arguments; last completed capture    Units: words / bytes / transitions
entries.description: WFScript extension: reports requested/returned 16-bit word count, requested BYTES, optional SDK valid-sample count and state, and first/second-half DIO0..5 activity. Zero activity is valid for an idle input. The SDK data API accepts bytes, not sample count; this is fixed in 5.6.49.2.

entries.name: Logic1.samples
entries.description: Returns complete sample words after a successful wait(). Each bit corresponds to one DIO pin (0..15).

entries.name: Logic1.Time.Rate.value
entries.args: Sample rate in Hz    Units: Hz
entries.description: SDK reads the native DigitalIn clock and rounds to a positive integer divider. Rate.real and Logic1.sampleRateHz show effective sampling rate after single().

entries.name: Logic1.Time.Rate.real
entries.description: Effective DigitalIn sample frequency from device clock divided by configured integer divider.

entries.name: Logic1.Time.Samples.value
entries.args: 16..32768 samples, subject to device limit    Units: samples
entries.description: v5.6.47 bounded single capture; requests larger than hardware DigitalIn buffer are rejected.

entries.name: Logic1.sampleRateHz
entries.description: Actual digital acquisition sample rate after Logic1.single(). Use this value for plot timebase.

entries.name: Protocol1.stop
entries.description: Releases the protocol-owned DWF digital output engine and stops digital input. Never silently displaces Patterns, Logic or StaticIO. Always call stop in onShutdown or use panel native cleanup.

entries.name: Protocol1.status
entries.description: Reports active native protocol and configured states; Simulation has no hardware activity.

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.configure
entries.args: tx/rx distinct DIO 0..15; parity none/even/odd/mark/space; stopBits 0.5..2    Units: baud
entries.description: Uses native FDwfDigitalUart* functions. Requires common GND and safe 3.3V logic levels. Separate RX initialization via startRx/Receiver; no automatic UART line decoder.

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.startRx
entries.description: Initializes native receiver with a zero-length buffer; then poll read()/ReceiveArray().

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.write
entries.description: Binary-safe, sends zero bytes; simulates no hardware traffic.

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.writeText
entries.description: Converts to UTF-8; for arbitrary binary data use write().

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.read
entries.description: Manual mode reads the DWF SDK directly (unchanged). Automatic mode drains the native bounded queue without a second SDK reader. Queued data survives stopAutoRx until read or Protocol1.stop().

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.startAutoRx
entries.args: 2..1000 ms, queue 1024..1048576 bytes    Units: ms; bytes
entries.description: Starts native QTimer polling on PanelRuntime's QJSEngine worker thread. Drains the DWF receiver into a bounded queue; does not depend on JavaScript timers. Call configure() first. Cannot run during blocking JavaScript.

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.stopAutoRx
entries.description: Stops the Qt timer but retains SDK UART configuration. Protocol1.stop() releases digital resources. After stopping, read() drains any queued bytes before direct SDK reads.

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.onData
entries.description: Registers one optional JS callback, invoked on the QJSEngine thread after a native poll. Receives a copy, never consumes the read() queue. Timestamp is host-poll time, not bit-edge time. Callback exceptions use Panel diagnostics.

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.clearOnData
entries.description: Removes JS receive callback. Native UART Terminal display and receive queue continue independently.

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.available
entries.description: Number of unread bytes in WFScript's native queue. Returns 0 when in manual SDK mode or no queued data.

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.stats
entries.description: Cumulative receive statistics for the configured session. SDK overflow and WFScript application-queue drops are counted separately.

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.autoReceiving
entries.description: Native UART receiver poll timer running.

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.Receiver
entries.description: WaveForms-style alias for startRx().

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.Receive
entries.description: WaveForms-style text receive; reads up to 4096 bytes and decodes as UTF-8.

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.ReceiveArray
entries.description: WaveForms-style binary receive alias. Maximum 4096 bytes per call.

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.Send
entries.args: Text and optional LF append    Units: UTF-8
entries.description: WaveForms-style alias. Only LF ending supported here; full application line-ending GUI not implemented.

entries.name: Protocol1.UART.SendArray
entries.args: Byte array and optional LF    Units: bytes
entries.description: WaveForms-style send with optional LF.

entries.name: Protocol1.SPI.configure
entries.args: Four distinct DIO 0..15; optional dq2/dq3, duty and delays    Units: Hz
entries.description: Native master only. Supports 1/2/4 data lanes; select toggling may be host-controlled, not cycle-exact. Passive SPI Spy and slave emulation require separate implementations.

entries.name: Protocol1.SPI.transfer
entries.args: Integer word array; count; 1..32 bits; lane count 0/1/2/4    Units: words
entries.description: For large numbers split transfers or use command(); support bounded 65536 words. Simulation returns marked synthetic zeros.

entries.name: Protocol1.SPI.command
entries.args: Command 1..8 bits, 0..1024 dummy cycles; data words    Units: bits
entries.description: FDwfDigitalSpiCmdWriteRead family; command/dummy native SDK operation.

entries.name: Protocol1.SPI.Start
entries.description: WaveForms-style manual chip select assert. Call Stop afterward.

entries.name: Protocol1.SPI.Stop

entries.name: Serial.ports

entries.name: SerialConnection.on

entries.name: SerialConnection.write
entries.description: Writes up to 65536 bytes per call. No implicit serial port open.

entries.name: SerialConnection.open
entries.description: Explicitly opens the COM port. open callback runs on the next event-loop turn; native open failure throws. close() releases it.

entries.name: SerialConnection.off
entries.description: Removes all listeners for the specified event; no implicit close.

entries.name: SerialConnection.close

entries.name: SerialConnection.info

entries.name: TCP.create
entries.args: Destination DNS hostname or IP; TCP port 1..65535
entries.description: TCP client based on QTcpSocket, event-driven. write() accepts UTF-8 string or number[] bytes. Data events may contain partial messages; on('line') assembles LF lines.

entries.name: TCP.createServer
entries.description: Native QTcpServer. Explicit listen. Binding to 0.0.0.0 exposes the socket on the network; localhost is the safe default. TCP client event receives a full connection wrapper.

entries.name: TCPConnection.on
entries.args: data (legacy byte[]), binary (native BinaryBuffer), line, connect, error, close
entries.description: Events are opt-in. TCP is a byte stream; callback chunks do not equal messages. Use Binary.stream() to frame bytes. Existing data handlers remain compatible.

entries.name: TCPConnection.write
entries.args: String, array of bytes, or native BinaryBuffer
entries.description: Writes up to 65536 bytes per call, bounded 256 KiB queue. Native write does not create a JS byte array. TCP is still a byte stream.

entries.name: TCPConnection.connect
entries.description: Nonblocking QTcpSocket.connectToHost. connection/error events arrive asynchronously; no timer polling.

entries.name: TCPConnection.close
entries.description: Aborts and releases socket. Default server is bound to localhost until explicitly configured otherwise.

entries.name: TCPConnection.info
entries.description: Read-only state, peer/local ports and byte counts.

entries.name: TCPServer.on
entries.description: Incoming QTcpSocket is assigned an independent connection object. Register its events inside the handler.

entries.name: TCPServer.listen
entries.description: Only listens when invoked. port:0 allows OS to choose an ephemeral port for local self-tests.

entries.name: TCPServer.close
entries.description: Stops listening. Already-accepted connections have their own handles and close automatically at Panel shutdown.

entries.name: TCPServer.info
entries.description: Returns bound local TCP port, open/listening state and counters.

entries.name: UDP.create

entries.name: UDPConnection.on

entries.description: UDP datagram boundaries are preserved. binaryMessage carries native buffer + sender info; legacy message remains.

entries.name: UDPConnection.send
entries.description: UDP has 65507-byte max datagram and preserves message boundaries.

entries.name: UDPConnection.bind
entries.description: Opt-in bind to localhost port 0 by default. To accept traffic from other hosts, explicitly set host:'0.0.0.0'.

entries.name: UDPConnection.close
entries.description: Stops receiving and releases the socket. Automatic cleanup on Panel shutdown.

entries.name: UDPConnection.info
entries.description: Returns local bound UDP port and byte counters.

entries.name: Binary

entries.name: Binary.create

entries.name: Binary.fromHex

entries.name: Binary.fromArray

entries.name: Binary.fromUtf8

entries.name: Binary.fromBase64

entries.description: Bounded append for small log files. Not atomic relative to crashes; 2 MiB cap.

entries.name: FileIO.readJson
entries.description: Throws on invalid JSON. Top-level object or array.

entries.name: FileIO.writeJson
entries.args: JSON-compatible object or array    Units: JSON
entries.description: Atomic replacement, pretty JSON. No file written until called.

entries.name: FileIO.readCsv
entries.description: Quoted comma, embedded newline and escaped quote support; returns strings.

entries.name: FileIO.writeCsv
entries.args: Array of row arrays    Units: CSV
entries.description: Atomic replacement. Each CSV cell is quoted as required.

entries.name: FileIO.readBytes
entries.description: Returns unsigned byte values 0..255; 2 MiB limit.

entries.name: FileIO.writeBytes
entries.args: Approved file and array of unsigned bytes    Units: bytes
entries.description: Atomic binary write. Rejects invalid byte values.

entries.name: Tool.question
entries.description: Asynchronous Qt dialog; callback runs on Panel QJSEngine thread. No modal wait in JavaScript.

entries.name: Tool.getText
entries.description: Operator edit; cancellation gives accepted=false.

entries.name: Tool.getNumber
entries.description: Native Qt floating input, not blocking JS.

entries.name: Tool.getItem
entries.description: Selection dialog.

entries.name: Tool.getOpenFile
entries.description: Explicitly grants read permission to selected file for current Panel run.

entries.name: Tool.getSaveFile
entries.description: Explicitly grants read/write permission for chosen file for current Panel run.

entries.name: Database.open
entries.args: Simple database filename (no folders); callback(result) with {ok,db,path,error}
entries.description: Optional Qt QSQLITE driver required. Asynchronous on a dedicated database thread. Creates database in shared PanelData directory; other trusted Panels may open the same database file. At most 4 databases per Panel. Nothing opens automatically on startup.

entries.name: Database.exec
entries.args: Open database handle, SQL, parameter array, callback(result)
entries.description: Prepared SQL binds parameters (not string concatenation). Supports INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and ordinary CREATE/DROP/ALTER TABLE or INDEX. Only one statement per request; no ATTACH, PRAGMA, VACUUM, triggers or multi-statement SQL. Callback result {ok,changes,insertId,error}.

entries.name: Database.query
entries.example: Database.query(db,'SELECT t,v FROM samples ORDER BY t DESC LIMIT 20',[],function(r){if(r.ok)ui.set('resultsTable',r.rows);});
entries.args: Open handle, SELECT statement, bound parameters and callback
entries.description: Callback {ok,columns,rows,rowCount,error}, where rows are actual JavaScript arrays of arrays. Max 250 rows / 16 columns, text cell limit 4096 chars. Use the existing Experiment Data Table widget with matching column headers.

entries.name: Database.close
entries.description: Connections and pending JavaScript callbacks are cleaned up automatically on Panel shutdown. Queries and writes are queued and serialized on a dedicated QThread, not the AD3 worker.

entries.name: TestRunner.configure
entries.description: Native C++ executive. totalTimeoutMs is a monotonic total-run deadline in milliseconds; 0 disables it. UI targets are optional. Timed execution uses one worker-thread Qt event loop, not a blocking wait.

entries.name: TestRunner.loadDefinition
entries.description: Manual-mode only for projects without a project-owned definition. Project-managed tests load automatically; do not call from operator script. Transactional C++ loader validates every step and resolves its handler/handlers names against callable exports. Replaces current steps/config only when all entries pass. Manual TestRunner.add() remains supported. Setup/Main/Cleanup ordering remains native; no JS eval or second engine.

entries.name: TestRunner.loadDefinitionFile
entries.args: Existing file ending .wftest.json (max 128 KiB), imported .mjs module
entries.description: Read and validate a versioned standalone JSON sequence file. Only the data file is loaded from disk; functions must already be exported by a separately loaded module. No file writes and no test execution occur on import. Invalid files preserve the previous executable sequence.

entries.name: TestRunner.saveDefinition
entries.args: Existing parent folder, destination ending .wftest.json    Units: UTF-8 JSON
entries.description: Explicitly export the most recently imported declarative definition atomically using QSaveFile. Rejects active executions, unsupported filename extensions and sequences assembled with manual add() calls. Saves configuration and named handlers, never source code or runtime results.

entries.name: TestRunner.definition
entries.args: No arguments    Units: Versioned JSON-like sequence
entries.description: Read-only snapshot of the imported data-only definition; empty for sequences assembled exclusively with TestRunner.add(). Does not contain callable functions. Changes to runtime options through configure() do not rewrite the source definition.

entries.name: TestRunner.add
entries.description: Manual-mode only when no native project testDefinition is loaded. For normal project tests use the Visual Editor. Numeric steps can use scalar limits {low,high}, or named measurements: {vpp:{name:'Amplitude',low:1.9,high:2.1,unit:'Vpp'}} when returning a JSON object/array. v5.6.59: group=setup/main/cleanup (default main); C++ always executes Cleanup after failed/error Main tests. type=test (default, successful PASS) or action (successful DONE). Modes: once calls the function once; delay waits durationMs without calling JS; callback passes {id,name,params,token,runId} to its function and awaits TestRunner.complete/fail; poll calls {poll} on a best-effort Qt timer (intervalMs >= 10) until it returns true (PASS) or false (FAIL). Poll return undefined/null = pending. {start} runs once; {finish}(status,elapsedMs) runs at termination, including normal abort/reset when the engine is available. Callbacks may come directly from modules.load('...mjs') exports or included .js global functions. Synchronous hardware/JS calls cannot be force-preempted by a Qt timer.

entries.name: TestRunner.complete
entries.args: Unique callback token; number, JSON object/array, or action/test boolean
entries.description: RC1.5.10: callback completion supports finite scalar measurements (backwards compatible), JSON objects and arrays. For a numeric step define measurements with paths such as vpp, metrics.rms, channels[0], temperatures[*]; the native engine applies each low/high rule, writes separate Measurement Table entries, and retains the result in the JSON report. Extra JSON fields are metadata only. Structured results are limited to 32 KiB, arrays evaluated with [*] to 32 elements, and RC1.5.14.3 permits 100,000 total run measurements while retaining 100 per-step evaluations. Tokens reject stale/duplicate replies but do not cancel SCPI operations; verify output OFF in Cleanup. The shown operator reading is a working example for a callback-mode step; set numeric limits in the Visual Editor.

entries.name: TestRunner.fail
entries.args: Token for the active callback-mode step, error message string
entries.description: Reports a callback-mode step ERROR and follows native Cleanup policy. A stale token returns false and cannot alter the next step. Not a hardware emergency shutdown.

entries.name: TestRunner.isActive
entries.description: True only for the current live callback step before completion/STOP/timeout. Use before sending additional SCPI commands from asynchronous continuations. All JavaScript runs on the Panel worker thread.

entries.name: TestRunner.onFinished
entries.description: Native completion notification after the last step, failure, timeout, or abort. The callback runs on the Panel worker thread and may read summary()/results(), but must not start another run synchronously. Needed because timed run() returns before the final result.

entries.name: TestRunner.run
entries.description: Starts/continues native scheduling. For all-once sequences it retains synchronous behavior; for delay/poll steps true means accepted/running, NOT final PASS. Inspect state() later or register onFinished(). Explicit callback-mode completion is supported; returned Promises are not automatically awaited. No nested event loop.

entries.name: TestRunner.next
entries.description: Begins one step only. A poll/delay step remains RUNNING and completes on a Qt timer; next() is rejected while a step is active. Subsequent steps require another next() or run().

entries.name: TestRunner.measure
entries.args: Measurement name, finite value and inclusive bounds    Units: Depends on unit
entries.description: Native inclusive limit evaluation, bounded results and automatic updates to table, result card and event log. Only callable during an executing step callback; do not call repeatedly during every pending poll unless intentional.

entries.name: TestRunner.reset
entries.description: Clears results and restores PENDING steps. Can cancel a pending timed step; its finish handler is called with aborted before results are cleared. Cannot reset from inside an active callback.

entries.name: TestRunner.clear
entries.description: Discard registered steps as well as results, only while idle/not in a session.

entries.name: TestRunner.abort
entries.description: Emergency abort between scheduled callbacks. The active step's finish handler runs when safe, but the sequence Cleanup group is skipped. Prefer terminate() for normal operator stops. Native Panel Stop interrupts the engine and cannot forcibly cancel a blocking driver call.

entries.name: TestRunner.terminate
entries.description: Cooperative stop: after the active callback returns, skip remaining Main steps and run the Cleanup group; the overall state is aborted. This is the preferred operator Stop for hardware test stations. Different from abort(), which stops immediately and skips sequence-level Cleanup.

entries.name: TestRunner.setRunInfo
entries.args: Legacy/dynamic tests: up to 16 primitive fields. Project-defined Run Information uses the native UUT widget instead.
entries.description: C++ owns a bounded snapshot of this run's UUT/operator/station metadata. Values must be primitive strings, booleans or finite numbers. Fields are included in summary().runInfo and report().runInfo, not persisted to .wfpanel. Cannot change during execution. reset()/clear() remove previous run metadata; start a new run with setRunInfo() again.

entries.name: TestRunner.runInfo
entries.description: Frozen native C++ snapshot of current or last execution; not changed when editing next UUT.

entries.name: TestRunner.pendingRunInfo
entries.args: No arguments    Units: Pending UUT inputs
entries.description: Live pending operator values from the one project-owned model shared by all Run Information widgets. Includes hidden Pages; no active widget. Numeric entries remain text until validated at run start. Does not overwrite report().runInfo for an already completed execution.

entries.name: TestRunner.setVariable
entries.description: Share a bounded primitive value between imported library step callbacks within the active C++ execution. Only valid inside a running step handler. Values are cleared on each run and reset; no JavaScript objects, functions or pointers are stored.

entries.name: TestRunner.variable
entries.description: Returns the native value recorded by setVariable() or undefined/invalid if absent; use for cross-step communication without module globals.

entries.name: TestRunner.variables
entries.args: No arguments    Units: Shared variable snapshot
entries.description: Returns all named C++-owned values shared between test steps in this execution. Included in report().variables.

entries.name: TestRunner.saveReport
entries.args: Absolute or relative existing folder and .json/.csv file name; format json or csv    Units: UTF-8
entries.description: Explicit export only after a completed run (PASS/FAIL/ERROR/ABORTED). JSON preserves the entire structured native report. CSV writes one STEP row per step and one MEASUREMENT row per measurement with linked stepId. Uses QSaveFile atomic replacement; parent directory must already exist. Does not run automatically on Panel load.

entries.name: TestRunner.exportReport
entries.example: const path=TestRunner.exportReport('json'); if(path) print('Saved:',path); else print(TestRunner.lastError);
entries.description: Creates Documents/WFScript Reports when explicitly invoked for a terminal run. File name contains a sanitized UUT ID plus the unique execution ID; returns saved path or an empty string on error. JSON is the complete record; CSV is a tabular step/measurement export. Never writes on Panel load or while a test is still RUNNING.

entries.name: TestRunner.archiveInfo
entries.args: No arguments; native automatic report storage    Units: Status / path
entries.description: Read-only status of the most recent automatic archive: idle, pending, disabled, saved or error. The project Test Sequence Editor > Report Storage owns auto-save and folder selection. A report is archived after all Cleanup finishes, even for failed/error/aborted executions. File failures do not change the test verdict. The onFinished handler can read archiveInfo(). No archive is written on Panel startup.

entries.name: TestRunner.report
entries.description: C++ owned run record: schemaVersion, executionId, title, state, startedAtUtc, finishedAtUtc, elapsedMs, summary, steps[] (group,type,status,timing), measurements[] (stepId, value, limits, status), runInfo, and per-run variables. Automatic archiving is configured in Test Sequence > Report Storage; use archiveInfo() to get the result path. Manual saveReport() and exportReport() remain available. Also includes a definition SHA-256 and execution mode when available.

entries.name: TestRunner.summary
entries.args: No arguments    Units: counts and ms
entries.description: Native snapshot includes total and active step elapsed ms, pollCount, currentStepId, totalTimeoutMs, completion counts, failure counts and lastError. Timed steps remain RUNNING between callbacks.

entries.name: TestRunner.results
entries.description: Native bounded measurement records {name,value,low,high,unit,stepId,status}; updates the existing Measurement Table. Transient runtime state, not persisted to .wfpanel.

entries.name: TestRunner.state
entries.description: idle/running/passed/failed/error/aborted. For timed tests, wait for onFinished or inspect the status after completion rather than reading it immediately after run().

entries.name: TestRunner.lastError
entries.description: Native validation errors, timeout messages and JavaScript handler exceptions; original module filename/line retained in diagnostics.
